# Didache Chapter 14 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_014_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 14

**1** On the Lord's Day, gather together, break bread and give thanks — having first confessed your transgressions so that your sacrifice may be pure.

**2** Anyone who has a dispute with a fellow believer must not join you until they have been reconciled — so that your sacrifice may not be defiled.

**3** For this is what the Lord spoke of: "In every place and at every time, offer me a pure sacrifice; for I am a great king, says the Lord, and my name is marvellous among the nations."

---

*LOGOS notes: Three short verses — but they contain an entire theology of Sunday worship. (1) The Lord's Day (κυριακή) is the Christian assembly day, replacing or standing alongside the Sabbath. (2) Communal confession (v.1) must precede the Eucharist — echoing ch. 4:14 and anticipating Justin Martyr's description of Sunday worship. (3) Interpersonal reconciliation (v.2) is a prerequisite — echoing Matt 5:23-24 ("leave your gift there before the altar and first go be reconciled to your brother"). (4) The Eucharist is explicitly called θυσία (sacrifice) — one of the earliest applications of this term to the Christian rite. (5) Malachi 1:11 is quoted as a prophecy now fulfilled in Christian worship — the "pure sacrifice" offered everywhere among the nations.*
